segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan walked over on his four massive paws, letting out a gentle, happy snort that blew confetti off Pip's head.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: With a soft, magical shimmer, Titan began to shrink.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His twenty-foot battle-frame melted away until he was back to his normal, cuddly, ninety-pound American Bulldog self. He flopped onto his belly across your legs with a contented groan, his little docked nub tail thumping the floor: thump-thump-thump.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Across the platform, the Clockmaker slowly sat up.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His obsidian watch was cracked and lifeless. He looked out through the shattered skylight at Everfrost, glowing with golden holiday warmth, the Great Clock singing its forward song.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For the first time in centuries, the cold, bitter sneer was gone from his face.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Tears traced lines through the soot on his cheeks.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the Clockmaker whispered, his hands trembling as he watched the gears turn.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I forgot... how beautiful tomorrow could be.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby walked over to his old master. He didn't raise his wrench. He didn't call the guards.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The broad-shouldered elf reached down with his calloused hand, helping the Clockmaker to his feet.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby said softly, his braided beard brushing his chest.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You just forgot that Christmas isn't meant to be trapped. It's meant to lead us forward.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Come on, master. Let's go home. Granny has a warm plate of cookies waiting on the hearth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Clockmaker bowed his head, wiping his tears with his velvet sleeve, and let his old apprentice lead him toward the lift.
